declarations.coverage: This repository has exactly one documentation root, `docs`, with the usage, development, and adr categories populated and an agents category that is mostly exact-owned. The confirmed paths are every Markdown document in that tree except the four exact-owned shared agent configuration files, plus the repository-root glossary `CONTEXT.md` and the two root decision records `authoring-notes.md` and `design-review.md` that the documentation links. `docs/README.md` and the three category `README.md` files make the root recognizable to the read-only check. No document moves and no link repair is needed: the preparation change already rewrote the two broken wayfinder links, and the tree is already categorized. The retained non-Markdown artifacts under `docs`, the review drafts, the source-side guidance and discovery instructions, the vendored material, the exact-owned shared files, and the Repository README are excluded with individual reasons below.

declarations.coverage: This declaration changes only remote GitHub configuration through its two authored fixes, so its project-content scope is intentionally empty. The repository identity is unambiguous: the single `origin` remote is `https://github.com/lutzseverino/repo-canon`, the repository this adoption runs in and whose labels, required check, and merge settings the maintainer authorizes.

This repository is a single standards source with one root manifest and one set of development commands, and it has no nested Project. Every nested directory is either vendored third-party material, declared source content, tests and fixtures, retained documentation, or organizational. There is therefore no non-root Project README to propose, and the scope is intentionally empty.

declarations.content:
# Discover documentation scope

Inspect every existing documentation root, documentation link, domain glossary,
context map, and project-specific agent guidance. Identify the individual files
needed to categorize documentation under usage, development, adr, and agents;
provide a short README for each populated documentation directory; keep the
root documentation map and the required `docs/development/README.md`; preserve
useful material; and repair links affected by any move.

Propose individual paths for every existing source, intended destination,
directory README introduction, glossary or context map that needs work,
`docs/agents/project.md` when repository-specific constraints require it, and
file whose links need repair. For a missing file, provide absence evidence plus
positive evidence for its owning topic or Project. Record each relevant
candidate as included or excluded with a reason, explain complete coverage, and
disclose unresolved questions.

Represent each applicable documentation root with its root `README.md` path and
the `README.md` path of at least one directly nested usage, development, adr, or
agents category when that root has content. This lets the read-only operation
distinguish a root at an arbitrary location from an ordinary nested directory
index. If the confirmed individual paths cannot make that distinction, leave
the root question unresolved rather than guessing that structural coverage is
complete.

Do not propose directory trees or globs. Keep the exact-owned shared files
`docs/agents/README.md`, `docs/agents/domain.md`,
`docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`, and `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` outside this
scope. Keep all other declarations' paths disjoint. A move requires authority
for its source, destination, and affected link repairs.

# Discover GitHub repository configuration scope

This declaration changes only remote GitHub configuration through its authored
operations. Propose no project-content paths or directories. Explain that the
empty contextual scope is intentional and disclose any unresolved uncertainty
about the repository identity or whether remote configuration is authorized.

The complete inspection still presents the operations and their prerequisites
before confirmation. Empty project-content scope does not authorize a remote
mutation by itself.

# Discover Project README scope

Inspect the complete repository evidence for maintained Projects: manifests,
workspace and build configuration, existing documentation, maintained source,
and meaningful component boundaries. A Project is a maintained app, service,
library, or tool with its own responsibility and development commands,
including internal packages. Directory names and conventional layouts alone do
not establish membership. Exclude fixtures, generated output, and directories
that only organize other content.

Propose one individual non-root `README.md` path for every Project. Include an
existing README when present. For a missing README, include its intended path
with absence evidence and positive evidence for the Project. Record each
relevant candidate as included or excluded with a reason, explain how the paths
cover every Project, and disclose unresolved membership questions. Do not
propose directory trees, globs, the root README, exact-owned files, or paths
owned by another declaration.
